items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: A fella by the name of Hank Halstead had the band down there.

ctx.x: Well, some of the earlier things he did, as you heard, were very melodic, lyrical.

Later, he got more frenzied as he got into another kind of music. Well, you changed like that. I've seen bands do that. I've seen bands make a national reputation playing one style. And the minute they get in the money, they changed the band around and play all together different. And it synced. Kenton is one that did that. He got more wild and more wild as he was. There's a funny thing about Kenton. I was out in California in 1934 to 1938 with Gene Austin. And I went down to Balboa Beach. And there had a bunch…

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Stan was just club dating around. He had been working with Hank Hal Halstead you know and they weren't doing anything.

ctx.x: Oh, I know where we were. We were talking about the men in the band. You were going to tell us. Yeah. You took Candy's place.

Yeah, well, I took Candy went with, I took your cigarette. Yeah, Candy Candido, he quit to go with Ted Fiorita. And that's when Gene sent for me. And at the time, I was part owner of a nightclub. Out here, originally it was the Honeysuckle, and then it got to be the Golden Pumpkin. And the place in there, it was a summer place. It drew good in the summer. Winter wasn't no good at all because right under the lake it used to get a lot of fog out there. People wouldn't come out in the winter clubs. And they had to…

around $35 a week and I told them they didn't believe me. I told them I said well I didn't lie to you so far why should I lie to you about that? So it wound up that they fined Coco $250 and they fined a bass player $250 and Austin $1,000 and $1,100 they had to pay back. They didn't fined me a dime. So I got you know just by telling the truth I got by without having to pay anything. So with this place in the back that we played in the afternoon we played from 12 to 3.
